body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 16, 2026, and we’re starting the week with a high near 98° under clear skies. Overnight, a grass fire flared up near Nord Avenue and Hageman Road, drawing a battalion-sized response, while the rest of the county saw a string of disturbances. Air quality is good at an AQI of 48, and no weather alerts are active.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most notable call came just after 2:20 a.m., when reports of flames at Nord Avenue and Hageman Road brought Engine 67, Engine 65, Truck 65, and Battalion 6 to the northwest side. The field, known for bonfires, saw about a half-acre of brush and grass burning. Crews called for an additional engine, and an Edwards Air Force Base water tender was offered as backup. The fire was contained to the field with no structures threatened.

Elsewhere in Kern County, deputies and officers handled a series of disturbances. Around 10:54 p.m., a vehicle fled into a dirt field near Morning Drive, prompting Air 1 to circle overhead. Around 11:28 p.m., a caller reported 150 to 250 vehicles gathering in a furniture store parking lot, drawing multiple units and a request for Air 1. At about 10:35 p.m., a disturbance involving five to six subjects, including a female reportedly displaying a taser, unfolded at a garbled location. Shortly before 1 a.m., a caller in a white van west of the AM/PM on Highway 119 reported subjects attempting to attack him, and deputies checked the area.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 70° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is good at an AQI of 48. Skies will be clear throughout the day.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** a man was arrested in Bakersfield following a domestic violence standoff that involved minors. The Bakersfield Police Department said the incident unfolded in a neighborhood where officers worked to safely evacuate the children and bring the suspect into custody. The arrest highlights ongoing challenges in addressing domestic violence cases in the city.

**According to 23ABC,** Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs shared Fourth of July findings at a recent meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents. Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, noted that the holiday brought serious injuries and fatalities statewide from fireworks. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, city officials say stronger policies are in the works to further deter illegal fireworks use.

**23ABC also told us that** Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, recently traveled to San Diego to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with federal agencies to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development.

**KGET 17 announced that** Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal that would place Kern and dozens of other counties in a new state, separate from coastal California. Kern County District 3 Supervisor Jeff Flores said the effort is about making sure the region’s industries and way of life are taken seriously by state leaders. An analysis presented to the board found the proposed inland state would account for only about 15 percent of California’s current real GDP. CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart said that number tells a stark story about what separation would actually mean for the region.

## Something good

Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports will receive a portion of $109 million in federal aviation funding. This financial support will enhance local aviation infrastructure and services, benefiting residents and businesses across Kern County.

## Coming up this week

Here’s what’s on tap for the week ahead in Kern County:

On Tuesday, August 17, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m. The Historic Preservation Commission convenes at 4:00 p.m., and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets at 2:00 p.m.

On Wednesday, August 18, the Water Board meets at 10:00 a.m.

On Thursday, August 19, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m.

Looking ahead to the weekend, mark your calendars for these events at the Fox Theater:

- On Saturday, August 21, Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio take the stage.

- On Thursday, August 26, Rodney Carrington performs.

- On Friday, August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE brings the beats.

- On Saturday, August 28, Willie Barcena brings the laughs.

- On Sunday, August 29, Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix pays homage to the King of Pop.

- On Friday, September 3, MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA takes the stage.

That’s your Monday morning brief. Enjoy the day, and we’ll see you right back here tomorrow.
